name: Model Weight Security
summary: The lab protects the weights that it has not released against theft by well-funded attackers, including states, and keeps dangerous weights closed.
description: Stolen weights remove all of a lab's safeguards at once. Published weights cannot be protected, so this covers weights before release and weights that the lab keeps closed. Open-weight labs are not marked down for what they publish.

criteria.label: State-Level Security
criteria.description: Security that aims to stop state attackers (RAND security level 4 or higher) for unreleased frontier weights.

criteria.label: Insider Controls
criteria.description: Controls against theft of unreleased weights by insiders, such as two-person access and few people with access.

criteria.label: Release Gate
criteria.description: A rule set in advance keeps a model's weights closed when the model passes a risk threshold.

orgs.summary: OpenAI protects unreleased weights with encryption and multi-party approval; its frameworks gate weight releases on risk tests, with no state-level security goal.

events.title: Signs White House pledge on weight security
events.summary: Signs the White House voluntary commitments, which include limiting model weight access by job function and an insider threat detection program for unreleased weights.

quote.text: This includes limiting access to model weights to those whose job function requires it and establishing a robust insider threat detection program consistent with protections provided for their most valuable intellectual property and trade secrets.

sources.title: Ensuring Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy AI
Fact Sheet: Biden-Harris Administration Secures Voluntary Commitments from Leading Artificial Intelligence Companies to Manage the Risks Posed by AI

events.title: Requires third-party audits of security controls
events.summary: Preparedness Framework version 2 lists security controls for High capability models, including strictly limited weight access and regular validation by third-party auditors.

events.title: Tests fine-tuned open weights before gpt-oss release
events.summary: Says it fine-tuned gpt-oss-120b as an attacker might and found it did not reach High capability under the Preparedness Framework. Three outside expert groups reviewed the method.

quote.text: These findings informed our decision to release the gpt-oss models.

events.title: Describes weight protections in SB 53 framework
events.summary: The Frontier Governance Framework describes encryption, monitoring and multi-party approval for unreleased weights, with SOC 2 Type II audits and ISO 27001 certification.

quote.text: Model weights are protected through encryption (at rest and in transit), continuous monitoring, and access controls (e.g., multi-factor authentication, multi-party approval, and detailed logging).

sources.title: OpenAI Frontier Governance Framework
SB-53 Artificial intelligence models: large developers

state-level.commitment: Encryption, monitoring and outside audits for weights.
state-level.missing: No stated goal to stop state attackers found.

insider-controls.commitment: Multi-party approval, multi-factor authentication, logging and personnel screening.
insider-controls.missing: SOC 2 audit reports are not public.

release-gate.commitment: No deployment above acceptable risk; open weights tested after attacker fine-tuning.
release-gate.missing: No explicit rule to keep weights closed; OpenAI sets risk limits.

events.title: Sets ASL-3 security goal against non-state attackers
events.summary: The Responsible Scaling Policy requires ASL-3 security so that non-state attackers are unlikely to steal weights, and states cannot without significant expense.

quote.text: non-state attackers are unlikely to be able to steal model weights, and advanced threat actors (e.g. states) cannot steal them without significant expense

sources.title: Responsible Scaling Policy, Version 1.0

events.title: Adds security audits and state-level expectation
events.summary: Version 2.0 adds independent validation and expert red-teaming of security, and says AI R&D thresholds will likely need protection against theft by state-level adversaries.

quote.text: we expect a higher security standard (which would protect against model-weight theft by state-level adversaries) will be required

sources.title: Responsible Scaling Policy, Version 2.0

events.title: Excludes sophisticated insiders from ASL-3 security
events.summary: Version 2.2 removes sophisticated insiders and state-compromised insiders from the scope of the ASL-3 Security Standard.

sources.title: Responsible Scaling Policy, Version 2.2

events.title: Activates ASL-3 security protections
events.summary: Says it activated ASL-3 protections, including two-party authorization for weight access and binary allowlisting.

quote.text: Many of these controls, such as two-party authorization for model weight access, enhanced change management protocols, and endpoint software controls through binary allowlisting, are examples of following the best practices established by other security-conscious organizations.

sources.title: Activating AI Safety Level 3 protections

events.title: Covers weight protection in SB 53 framework
events.summary: Its SB 53 compliance framework covers how it protects model weights; the law requires a description of weight security practices.

quote.text: It also covers how we protect model weights and respond to safety incidents.

sources.title: Our compliance framework for California's SB 53

events.title: Turns higher security levels into public goals
events.summary: Version 3.0 keeps ASL-3 protections but makes higher security public goals, not hard commitments. RAND SL4-level security appears as an industry-wide recommendation.

quote.text: Rather than being hard commitments, these are public goals that we will openly grade our progress towards.

sources.title: Responsible Scaling Policy Version 3.0

state-level.commitment: ASL-3 aims to stop non-state attackers; RSP v3 names RAND SL4-level security as a goal.
state-level.missing: SL4-level security is a goal, not a hard commitment.

insider-controls.missing: ASL-3 excludes sophisticated and state-compromised insiders; no public outside audit found.

release-gate.commitment: Models past capability thresholds need ASL-3 security against weight theft.
release-gate.missing: Implied by the security rule, not stated; no outside check.

orgs.summary: Google's framework recommends weight security per capability level, up to RAND SL4 for ML R&D, but allows open release when benefits outweigh risks.

events.title: Defines security levels up to RAND L5
events.summary: The Frontier Safety Framework defines security levels from limits on unilateral weight access up to roughly RAND L4 and L5, but does not yet map them to thresholds.

quote.text: Higher level security mitigations result in greater protection against the exfiltration of model weights, and higher level deployment mitigations enable tighter management of critical capabilities.

sources.title: Introducing the Frontier Safety Framework
Frontier Safety Framework

events.title: Recommends RAND SL4 for ML R&D thresholds
events.summary: Version 2.0 recommends security near RAND SL4 for the top ML R&D level and SL2 for CBRN and cyber, and says the field as a whole must adopt them.

quote.text: We recommend security controls and detections at a level generally aligned with RAND SL 4 for this capability threshold, but emphasize that this must be taken on by the frontier AI field as a whole.

sources.title: Frontier Safety Framework 2.0
Updating the Frontier Safety Framework

events.title: Adds insider-threat security level for misuse risks
events.summary: Version 3.1 recommends Security Level 2+ for CBRN, cyber and manipulation levels, adding insider risk teams and background checks. It keeps an exception for open release when benefits outweigh risks.

quote.text: with additional security measures designed to address risks from insider threats and well-resourced non-state external actors

events.title: Limits access to high-risk model weights
events.summary: The Frontier AI Framework says access to high-risk models is limited to a few experts, with protections against exfiltration where feasible and commercially practicable.

quote.text: Access is strictly limited to a small number of experts, alongside security protections to prevent hacking or exfiltration insofar as is technically feasible and commercially practicable.

state-level.missing: No stated goal to stop state attackers; protections only where feasible and practicable.

events.title: Replaces no-release rule with deployment after mitigations
events.summary: Version 2 changes the high-risk measure from no release to deployment, including open release, once mitigations cut risk to moderate or lower. Version 2.1 in October 2026 keeps these terms.

quote.text: we will not deploy the model externally unless we have strong additional evidence that mitigations are sufficiently robust to adversarial attacks that the fully mitigated model is reduced to moderate or lower levels.
